title: King Henry I (“the Fowler”)
fact_summary: King of the East Franks and Saxons, father of Otto the Great. Widukind says he bought nine years of peace from the Hungarians and then beat them in 933.

claims.text: Widukind says the Hungarians again overran all Saxony while the king kept to the fortress of Werla, because he did not trust his raw soldiers against so fierce a people.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: He says a Hungarian leader was captured and brought to the king. The Hungarians offered great weights of gold and silver for him; the king refused the gold and asked for peace, and in return for the captive “with other gifts”, peace was fixed for nine years (ad novem annos pax firmaretur).
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: Widukind says that when the king had horsemen tested in battle he refused the Hungarian envoys their usual gifts, and put their army to flight near a place called Riade.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: The continuation of Regino's chronicle says: “King Henry laid the Hungarians low with great slaughter and captured many of them.”
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

claims.text: Liudprand says the king had his victory painted in the upper hall of a house at Merseburg.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

open_questions.text: The byname “the Fowler” does not appear in the passages read. Where does it come from, and how old is it?
In which years did the nine-year peace begin and end? Widukind gives no year.
